title: The Italian Passato Prossimo
explanation: The passato prossimo is the most commonly used past tense in Italian. It is a compound tense, meaning it is formed by combining an auxiliary verb—either avere (to have) or essere (to be)—with the past participle of the main verb. It is used to describe completed actions that happened at a specific point in the past or actions that have relevance to the present. For most transitive verbs, you use avere as the auxiliary, while intransitive verbs, especially those indicating movement, state of being, or reflexive actions, generally take essere.

examples.example: Ho mangiato una pizza ieri sera.
Siamo andati al cinema sabato scorso.
Maria ha comprato un libro nuovo.
